topStories.headline: Bond Dollars Are Rebuilding West Portal Elementary — But the Watchdog Committee Has Sued SFUSD
topStories.dek: Construction at the century-old school presses forward on a $21 million bond-funded project, even as the Citizens Bond Oversight Committee takes San Francisco Unified to court over how it governs bond spending.
topStories.body:
Work at West Portal Elementary is visibly accelerating: eight dilapidated portable classrooms have been cleared, two new buildings are rising, and a warming kitchen renovation is underway — all part of a $21 million project designed by WRNS Studio and built by general contractor Bana Builders. SFUSD project records show construction restarted in early 2024 after a delay caused by insufficient funds, drawing on state reimbursements to the district's 2016 bond program and additional money from the 2024 Prop A bond. West Portal is one of more than a dozen district schools receiving upgrades through the two bond measures.

In a report published this morning, KALW described Principal Pamela Aguilar giving a tour of the work and calling it "an epic transformation" of the school. Aguilar told the station that the school had made a point of involving students in the process — staff laminated pictures of the on-site construction equipment and posted them along the fence line so children could follow the progress. A vote by the SFUSD board earlier this week also directed additional bond funds toward student career development in the construction trades, according to KALW.

The renovation is unfolding against a contested backdrop. KALW reported today that SFUSD's Citizens Bond Oversight Committee — the independent panel required by California law to review bond expenditures and report its findings to the public — has filed suit against the district. The legal conflict traces to February 2026, when SFUSD adopted Administration Regulation 1225, a policy that critics say reduced the CBOC's independence by shifting oversight authority closer to the Board and Superintendent. CBOC vice chair Laurance Lee told KALW that part of the committee's work is catching accounting mistakes, a function members contend has been compromised by the new regulation.

West Portal Elementary turns 100 this year. Its centennial block party is scheduled for Saturday, October 3, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. on West Portal Avenue, starting at the West Portal Library courtyard.

topStories.headline: SF Good Neighbor Week Opens Friday — and a West Portal Resident Is Running It
topStories.dek: Julia Gitis, who lives in West Portal, is organizing the second annual SF Good Neighbor Week, a nine-day citywide celebration of community connection running September 26 through October 4.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Good Neighbor Week returns Friday for its second year, running September 26 through October 4. The holiday is modeled on National Good Neighbor Day, first proclaimed by President Jimmy Carter in 1978. It was brought to San Francisco last year by Julia Gitis, a West Portal resident, who organized the inaugural 2025 edition and is now expanding it as a citywide event.

The SF Examiner, in a story published today, described Gitis as staging the event to promote civic service and everyday acts of kindness between neighbors. The citywide kickoff is Friday, September 26, at noon at Civic Center Plaza, with a parade of neighborhoods. September 28 is National Good Neighbor Day itself.

The Greater West Portal Neighborhood Association is a participating group and has listed the week prominently on its website, encouraging residents to join events and use the occasion to meet people on their block or in their building. The sfgoodneighborweek.org website describes the celebration as organized into five tracks: making it official, the Good Neighbor Awards, neighborhood events, resources for block leaders, and technology and innovation. Neighborhood associations are encouraged to celebrate local nominees and host their own events through October 4.

moreNews.headline: Empire Theater Site Would Become West Portal's Largest-Ever Housing Project Under Plans Filed in Late August
moreNews.body: Developer DM Development, on behalf of property owner Empire West Portal LLC, filed revised plans in late August that nearly triple the proposed apartment count at 85 West Portal Avenue — growing the project from 64 to 172 units and from 9 to 12 stories. The expansion was enabled by Mayor Daniel Lurie's Family Zoning changes and the acquisition of an adjacent property at 61 West Portal Avenue, which currently houses a Goodwill store and a Supercuts. As reported by SFist on August 31 and The Real Deal on September 2, the revised proposal calls for 172 apartments — including 26 affordable units — plus roughly 7,000 square feet of ground-floor retail. The Empire Theater at the site closed in early 2021. DM Development's project page lists Handel Architects as the designer and projects a 2028 completion; city planning approval is still required.

moreNews.headline: Stonestown Redevelopment Enters Technical Mapping Phase After Infrastructure Financing Plan Approved January 27
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on January 27, 2026, to approve the Infrastructure Financing Plan for the Stonestown redevelopment project, according to a newsletter published by Brookfield Properties, the mall's developer. The vote established an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District, a state-authorized tool that directs a portion of new property tax revenue from future development back into local infrastructure and community benefits, including affordable housing, transportation improvements, open space, childcare, and a replacement senior center. Brookfield noted that the January approval does not authorize immediate construction; the project has entered a post-entitlement technical mapping phase. The underlying development plan, unanimously approved by the Board of Supervisors in July 2024, calls for up to 3,500 housing units and 160,000 square feet of new retail on approximately 27 acres of surface parking lots surrounding the existing mall, which will remain open throughout any future construction.

moreNews.headline: Lake Merced Trail: Skyline Boulevard Pathway Reopened September 4
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Recreation and Park Department posted an update on September 4, 2026, confirming that the pathway along Skyline Boulevard at Lake Merced is now open following trail work that had required a temporary pedestrian detour. The reopening is part of the department's ongoing Lake Merced Trail Improvement Project, which has included ADA parking upgrades, a National Fitness Campaign fitness court, new picnic tables and benches, trail signage, and landscaping improvements. Questions about the project can be directed to project manager Omar Davis at omar.davis@sfgov.org.
